chapter: Army and arrival in New Orleans
title: New Orleans musicians in his Army unit: Clowns Todd, Chiff, Paul Ben
summary: Fellow Army musicians including pianist Clowns Todd, trumpeter Chiff and trombonist Paul Ben.

blocks.x: Well, just Oscar Shields. There was about the three of us, oh no, what is I'm talking about? Clowns Todd, Chiff, there's a triumphant player named Ben. Ben, Ben something, he from off the river to a real Creole fellow. Ben, he named Ben, I can't think of his first name.
They call him Ben or something like that?

Yeah, Ben. His name must have been Benjamin but they called him Ben. But anyhow Clowns Todd was on piano, Chiff and me was on trumpets, and this Ben man, I can't think of his name. To tell you the truth I think the Moosef was from New Orleans but I just can't think of him now. But the Moosef was right out of New Orleans.
Well how did Clowns Todd play? What kind of piano?
He played nice, he played really nice.
Yeah, he's a pretty good reader.
Did he play ragtime tunes or blues or what?

Yeah, he played all that. Now that's a man doing some singing. He did very smart singing. But I didn't think much of his voice, I don't want to critic him or nothing, but I didn't think so much of his voice. But he used to sing though. And he's a lively fellow, he's long clothed for God.
Did you ever know Hank Benson? Sure, Hank Benson, trombone player. He worked with you, that's right. Yeah. It wasn't him on trombone in the Army though, huh?
No, he wasn't in the Army with me. If he was, I didn't know him then.
It was another Ben that played trombone then.
Paul Ben. Paul Ben, that's his name. Yeah. Paul Ben. I knew it would come to me.
